clue.text: Extra gear for minister some might say

indicators.note: signals that the vestment's name is spoken and heard as a different word

parts.note: a surplice is the white vestment worn by a clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman's spare outfit, described loosely by onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surplus is left over beyond what is needed, so it is additional or spare.

clue.text: In which one serves Scotch

definitions.meaning: a racket game where play begins with a serve
to scotch a rumour is to crush or quash it

explanation.surface: A drinks waiter pouring whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Squash is a racket sport begun by a serve, and to squash means to suppress.

clue.text: Level of game requiring more practice?

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game, so 'of game' gives RU'S
a tier is a level

explanation.surface: A tier of a sports competition where players need extra training.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of practice is rusty, and the comparative is one needing more training.

clue.text: Assortment of old army privates etc head for city

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, privates and the like

explanation.surface: A motley bunch of old soldiers marching to town.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic leader of a city is its chief, the head of the corporation.

clue.text: Recalled this writer's art in Paris Match

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the writer is I, and 'this writer's' reads as 'I am', I'M
French for 'thou art' is 'tu es'

explanation.surface: A writer remembers his article in the magazine Paris Match.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris Match is a French magazine, but 'Match' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-final, a match before the final.

clue.text: Snap warning to one intending to grasp a coffee?

definitions.meaning: a snap is a photograph, here the police photo of a suspect's face

definitions.text: warning to one intending to grasp a coffee?
definitions.meaning: read as a caution that the cup holding the coffee is scalding to the touch

explanation.surface: A sharp word of caution to someone reaching for their coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as MUG'S HOT, a warning about a hot cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A police photograph of a suspect's face is a snap, a quick photo.

clue.text: Factory engineer's the perfect husband, taking sick wife for first run!

indicators.note: taking in a replacement for a letter
the substitute goes in place of the earlier of two letters

parts.note: Mr Right is the ideal partner
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
ill means sick

explanation.surface: An ideal husband takes his unwell wife out for her first jog.
explanation.walkthrough: MR RIGHT has two R's; ILL W replaces the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A millwright builds and maintains mill machinery, an engineer in a factory.

clue.text: Mathematician's turn was first to come up

parts.note: a go is a turn

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means reading upwards

parts.note: led means was in front

explanation.surface: A mathematician took his turn and came top.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Gödel was the logician famous for his incompleteness theorems.

clue.text: Cobbler's chap with right fit, on reflection

parts.note: he is a man

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards

parts.note: able means fit

explanation.surface: A shoe-mender's man has good fit, after consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel bar is a small shop doing quick shoe repairs, a cobbler's shop.

clue.text: Prompter to sit keeping watch? On the contrary

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside
reverses who holds whom: the watch holds the sitting word

parts.note: a timer is a watch
to lie is to sit or be placed

explanation.surface: A theatre prompter sits keeping watch, or so we think.
explanation.definitionFit: Timely means prompt, so the comparative means more prompt, punctual.

clue.text: Stuff leaked by international body's decoded

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, so its possessive gives UN'S
to stuff is to cram
something that leaked has bled, as dye bleeds

explanation.surface: Material leaked by the United Nations turns out to have been decrypted.
explanation.definitionFit: A message that has been decoded has had its jumbled cipher put back into plain order.

clue.text: Maybe object to fell race's last fifty miles

indicators.note: the final letter of the word race is taken

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An objection to running the last fifty miles of a fell race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the hill-running sense next to 'race', but it means to cut down; a tree is something to fell.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree, such as this one, is a typical thing a forester might fell, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Elegantly move a very short distance in retiring

indicators.note: the measurement sits inside the word meaning retiring

parts.note: retiring means shy, reserved
one millimetre, written 1 mm, read as I MM

explanation.surface: A shy person edges gracefully forward by the tiniest amount.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1 mm becomes the letter I, a usual crossword swap.
explanation.definitionFit: To shimmy is to glide or sway smoothly, a graceful sliding motion.

clue.text: Like some supermarket goods, with in short just the first to be dispatched

indicators.note: the letter for with is placed inside the shortened word
short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: just means only, merely
Abel, killed by Cain, was the first person in the Bible to be murdered

explanation.surface: Supermarket goods sent out in a hurry, first in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims ONLY to ONL; 'in' puts W inside it. 'Dispatched' means killed, not sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops sell goods under their own brand name, a store's private label.

clue.text: The French go putting piece of toast in batter? Not only that

indicators.note: putting one word into another
the bread goes inside the French word

parts.note: aller is French for go
a round is a slice of toast

explanation.surface: A French chef puts toast into batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like cooking but is a cricketer; one who also bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who both bats and bowls well does more than just bat.

clue.text: Carry a rifle originally containing separate rounds for combatants

indicators.note: the letters are worked back into some other original arrangement

parts.note: two round letters O, set in at different places

explanation.surface: An instruction to soldiers to bear a rifle loaded with ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' says the two O's sit inside the rearranged letters of CARRY A RIFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The British air arm is a fighting force, a body of combatants in war.

clue.text: Dark circle light years above in front of galaxy

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits above the next

parts.note: fair means light, of hair or skin
YR is short for year
taken as written

indicators.note: the front of galaxy is its first letter

explanation.surface: Dark circle of space above a galaxy, light years away.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of dark grass caused by fungi, said in folklore to be made by fairies dancing.

clue.text: Familiar form of Queen missing Bottom in Shakespeare, creating storm

indicators.note: one word sits inside another

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare

indicators.note: the bottom (last) letter is lost

parts.note: Lizzy is a pet form of Elizabeth, the queen's name

explanation.surface: A queen's pet name lacking Bottom, a character from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, but it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm.

clue.text: Leaf container always kept within tree line

indicators.note: one word is held inside the other

parts.note: a larch is a conifer tree
ever means always
a file is a line, as in single file

explanation.surface: A container for leaves is placed inside a row of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is a sheet of paper, and this office binder holds loose sheets.

clue.text: Travel breaks girl organised: possible arrival in September

parts.note: Vi is a girl's name

indicators.note: one word breaks into another

parts.note: ran means organised
go means travel

explanation.surface: A girl's travel plans are organised for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in September is likely a Virgo, under the virgin sign.

clue.text: Take the liberty of involving ladies in future, maybe topless

indicators.note: involving means taking inside
topless means losing the top, and in a down answer the top is the first letter

parts.note: the future is a tense in grammar
the ladies is a toilet, a lav

explanation.surface: Making free with women in a future that may be topless.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone of their liberty is to make a slave of them.

clue.text: In different places, you'd be cheered

indicators.note: the letters are put in different places

explanation.surface: Wherever you go you would be welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be buoyed up is to be cheered, lifted in spirit.

clue.text: None of us can be heard when attack begins?

parts.note: none means nought, nil

indicators.note: signals that the word for of us is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A battlefield where nobody dares to make a sound before the assault.
explanation.definitionFit: The time set for an operation to start is its designated moment, the military term for launch.

clue.text: Sailor's hauled on line, composing shanty

parts.note: hove is the nautical past tense of heave

explanation.surface: A sailor hauls on a line while singing a sea song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shanty' suggests a sea song, but here it means a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude dwelling, a shack.

clue.text: Cases from umpteenth Yank to return across American island

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the abbreviation, lying across it
to return is to go back, so the letters are read backwards
the cases of each word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: An American heading back across the sea for the umpteenth time to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' means outer layers: each word's outside letters. 'to return' turns that pair round and 'across' sets it about the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyushu is the southernmost of Japan's four main islands.

clue.text: Good book for kid

definitions.meaning: .... is the abbreviation for the Book of Joshua in the Bible
to kid is to tease playfully

explanation.surface: A wholesome book for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease them good-naturedly, as is joshing.

clue.text: Flapping hood and retro clothes

indicators.note: retro means backwards-looking, so the letters run in reverse
the phrase clothes the letters, covering them inside it

explanation.surface: A flapping hood and old-fashioned garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, wrapping ODA inside 'hood and'; 'retro' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Flapping is fuss and agitation, as in 'in a flap', so a commotion.

clue.text: The forging of one copy with a drive?

definitions.text: The forging of one copy with a drive?

indicators.note: forging means hammering the letters into a new shape

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter making an illicit duplicate of a disc drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegally copying films is a kind of forgery, and the whole clue describes that crime.

clue.text: Take that doctor's stocking and suspender!

indicators.note: to stock is to hold, so the doctor is holding the other word inside

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor; the 's means is
a take on something is an angle, a point of view

explanation.surface: An exclamation about lingerie: a stocking and a suspender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' and 'suspender' look like underwear; one holds letters, the other means something that hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dangles hangs down, so it is suspended; a suspender here is anything that hangs.

clue.text: Daughter placed on corner small plant

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is added at the end, placed onto the rest

parts.note: to corner a market is to hog it
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A daughter puts a little plant in the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogweed is a tall umbelliferous weed, a type of plant.
